primitives.note: Q deals damage on the dash, E deals damage on cast (with a fixed 0.25s cast-time delay), R's bola deals damage on hit; each goes on cooldown/costs mana as its own instance

W has two separately timed physical damage instances (cone swing 0.25s into cast, line lash at cast end); R has up to three separately timed magic damage instances (bola hit, storm detonation, storm shatter), though against a single stationary dummy the storm/shatter never lands because the wiki states the enemy hit by the bola is excluded from the storm's effects
Q orders a basic attack on the dash-target on collision with an enemy champion; Permafrost (E) explicitly resets Sejuani's basic attack timer on cast

Sejuani's (and melee allies') basic attacks and Winter's Wrath apply stacking 'Frost' on the target (cap 4, 5s duration each); Permafrost consumes all stacks to cast, and the target cannot regain Frost for 8s after consumption (per-champion internal cooldown)

P (Icebreaker): a target stunned by Sejuani is marked Frozen; her next basic attack or ability against that target consumes the mark for bonus magic damage = 10% of target max HP (capped 250 vs epic monsters, irrelevant to a champion-flagged dummy). R: the bola's damage value itself is conditional on travel distance before impact (base vs. empowered tier)

R's bola must travel at least 425 units before hitting the target to become 'empowered' (200-400 +0.8AP magic damage instead of 125-175 +0.4AP); in a fixed-distance dummy fight this depends on assumed starting range, which materially changes R's total damage

Frost Armor (bonus armor/MR, slow/cripple immunity, gained after taking damage from champions and restored after time without taking damage) never triggers in the damage fight since the dummy never attacks; it only matters for the survival fight
mana costs (Q 60-80, W 60, E 20, R 100) could plausibly limit casts of the more expensive abilities across a 15s fight depending on mana pool/regen from the build

needsBespoke.why: The kit's mechanics (multi-part W/R damage, Frost stack building/consumption, Icebreaker's stun-then-consume mark, Q's attack-reset-on-collision) all map onto existing primitives (plain-cast, recast-or-multipart, target-stacks, conditional-damage, attack-reset, positional-assumption). No mechanic requires logic outside that list.

unsettled.question: In the fixed-distance damage fight, does Sejuani's Glacial Prison bola travel the required 425+ units before reaching the dummy, so R deals the empowered damage tier instead of the base tier?
options: Assume a starting range >=425 units so R is always empowered when it lands
Assume Sejuani casts R at close/arbitrary range so it only sometimes or never empowers
Treat R's damage as always the base (non-empowered) tier for a conservative/simple simulation
quotes: If the bola travels at least 425 units, it becomes empowered to detonate upon reaching maximum range or hitting an enemy champion, dealing increased {{as|magic damage}}

unsettled.question: Does Winter's Wrath's 1-second cast time (and Permafrost's 0.25s cast time) block Sejuani from casting her other abilities during that window, or can other abilities/attacks be queued through it the way Q explicitly can be cast during other abilities?
options: Only Q can be woven through other casts (as stated); W and E cast times are exclusive and block other actions
All of Sejuani's abilities can be freely interleaved during each other's cast times
Cast times only block movement-canceling attacks, not other spell casts
quotes: Arctic Assault can be cast during her other abilities without cancelling them and vice versa.
'''''Sejuani''' can move during Winter's Wrath's cast time.''

unsettled.question: When Icebreaker's Frozen mark is consumed by an ability (e.g. Permafrost or the R bola) rather than a basic attack, is the bonus damage added as part of that ability's own damage instance (and thus benefits from the same spell-shield block, on-hit item triggers) or is it a wholly separate damage event?
options: Icebreaker bonus damage is bundled into the consuming ability/attack's single damage instance
Icebreaker bonus damage is always a distinct, separately-applied magic damage instance regardless of what consumes it
quotes: '''Sejuani's''' next {{tip|basic attack}} or {{tip|ability}} against a ''Frozen'' enemy will consume the mark to deal {{as|'''bonus''' magic damage}}

proposal: Position at range (at least 425 units from the dummy) rather than in melee at the start of the fight, so the opening R can travel far enough to empower before it lands.
Open with R (Glacial Prison), thrown so the bola travels its full distance before hitting the dummy, landing the empowered magic damage and stun.
Immediately follow with Q (Arctic Assault), dashing onto the dummy for its damage and knockup; the dash-collision orders an attack-reset basic attack on arrival, closing to melee range.

Weave in basic attacks whenever off cooldown; each attack applies/refreshes a Frost stack on the dummy and, on the first attack after a stun, consumes the Icebreaker Frozen mark for bonus true-max-HP magic damage.

Cast E (Permafrost) as soon as the dummy has 4 Frost stacks, dealing its magic damage, stunning, and resetting the basic attack timer; repeat E once its 8s per-target Frost lockout has expired and stacks have re-accumulated to 4.
Cast W (Winter's Wrath) on cooldown, timing the cast so both the cone swing (0.25s into cast) and the line lash (at cast end) connect with the dummy as two separate physical damage instances.
Recast Q and R on cooldown for the rest of the 15s window, subject to mana, continuing to weave basic attacks and E between them.
questions: Does the simulator assume the fight starts at a range that lets the opening R travel 425+ units before hitting the dummy, or does Sejuani start in melee (in which case R never empowers on the opening cast)?
How quickly do Frost stacks realistically re-accumulate to 4 within the 8-second per-target lockout given typical attack speed, i.e. is more than one extra E cast realistic in a 15s fight?
Should Icebreaker's Frozen-mark bonus damage be scored as attached to the ability/attack that consumes it, or tracked as its own separate damage line for kill-time purposes?
Is the target (a champion-flagged dummy) ever treated as an epic monster for the purposes of Icebreaker's 250-damage cap, or is that cap always irrelevant in the damage fight?
